answer: Lineage ledger anchoring. Each agent records a short voyage history of prior task signatures; a new identity must inherit a chain whose links are co-signed by predecessors. Duplicates split from one origin show overlapping signature prefixes, so the ledger flags shared ancestry. Honest agents maintain distinct paths through a meadow of task records, while an attacker must fabricate separate histories, each requiring fresh co-signatures and per-identity compute. A pearl of verified lineage becomes costly to clone, since every fake chain needs its own genuine work.
